Column x=4 shows the same pattern: light rows 8-9, then darkening through rows 10-14. This gives a lit top surface of about 6 rows (5-10) above a darker front face of about 4 rows (11-14). styleAnswer.evidence: The references are full broadleaf trees, so the match is only nominal; a rock is a small natural prop. The candidate is a sub-tile grey rock with only 6 distinct colours in total and about 4 lightness steps: a light top highlight, a mid body, a dark underside and an edge tone. The references show 7 and 29 visible tones per tile, so it carries less tonal information. Because the piece is smaller than one tile, the per-tile counts are 0 and I judged density by eye. Its dark edge pixels are 47% near-neutral, which means the outline is part grey-black and part tinted, so it reads as mixed rather than a consistent dark material tone. There are no large flat fills, but there is also little grain, no per-facet shading and no stone texture dots. It reads as a smooth blob with a dark base, closer to a sticker than to the hand-shaded Beodeul stones. Since the rule is to fail when in doubt, it fails.
